name: Bellam Atukulu

desc: బెల్లం అటుకులు. Andhra bellam atukulu: thick poha tossed in warm Thati Bellam palm jaggery syrup with coconut, cardamom and ghee. A 10-minute sweet, with tips and FAQs.

ingredients: ¼ tsp cardamom powder · 1 tsp ghee
steps: Rinse the poha in a sieve under running water for a few seconds, drain, and leave it for 5 minutes to soften.
Melt the palm jaggery with 2 tbsp water on a low flame, then strain it.
Add the poha, coconut and cardamom to the warm syrup and toss gently on a low flame for 1–2 minutes, until every flake is coated.
Finish with the ghee and cashews. Serve warm or at room temperature.
approved.meta: Use thick poha. Thin poha turns mushy in the syrup.

intro: Bellam atukulu is the 10-minute sweet of Telugu homes. It is the poha offered to Krishna on Krishnashtami, recalling Kuchela's gift, and it is also a quick sweet for children after school. The poha is only rinsed, never cooked in water, and then tossed in warm jaggery syrup.
Our Thati Bellam palm jaggery gives it a deep brown colour and a rich, slightly smoky sweetness. This recipe serves 2.
quick: Soften thick poha, toss it in warm palm jaggery syrup with coconut and cardamom, and finish with ghee.
te_line: మందపాటి అటుకులను కడిగి మెత్తబడనివ్వండి. గోరువెచ్చని తాటి బెల్లం పాకంలో కొబ్బరి, యాలకుల పొడితో కలిపి, చివరగా నెయ్యి వేయండి.
hi_line: मोटे पोहे को धोकर नरम होने दें, गुनगुनी ताड़ के गुड़ की चाशनी में नारियल और इलायची के साथ मिलाएँ, और आख़िर में घी डालें।

time_note: Prep includes 5 minutes for the rinsed poha to soften.
groups: or the crushed seeds of 2–3 pods
steps: Put the poha in a sieve and pick out any bits of husk.
Rinse the poha in a sieve under running water for a few seconds, drain, and leave it for 5 minutes to soften. It should feel soft when pressed, but not wet.
Grate the palm jaggery finely, breaking up any hard lumps.
Melt the palm jaggery with 2 tbsp water on a low flame, then strain it. Wipe the pan and pour the syrup back in.
If you are using cashews, fry them in a little ghee till golden.
Add the poha, coconut and cardamom to the warm syrup and toss gently on a low flame for 1–2 minutes, until every flake is coated. Use a light hand so the flakes do not break.
Take the pan off the heat as soon as the flakes are coated; longer cooking makes them chewy.
Finish with the ghee and cashews. Serve warm or at room temperature.
tips: Use thick poha. Thin poha turns mushy in the syrup.
Do not soak the poha in a bowl of water; a quick rinse is enough, or it turns soft and sticky.
Keep the syrup warm, not bubbling, when the poha goes in, so the flakes coat evenly.
variations: Cane jaggery: use the same amount of grated cane jaggery for a lighter colour and a caramel-like sweetness.
With milk: pour 2–3 tbsp warm milk over the finished poha for a softer sweet.
With sesame: add 1 tbsp roasted sesame seeds along with the coconut.
serving: Serve it as naivedyam on Krishnashtami, or as a quick sweet for children after school.
storage: Best eaten the day it is made. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat them the next day; the poha firms up as it stands.
faq: Which poha is best for bellam atukulu?
Thick poha (atukulu). It holds its shape in the warm syrup; thin poha turns mushy.
Can I make bellam atukulu with cane jaggery?
Yes. Use the same amount of grated cane jaggery (cheruku bellam). It turns lighter in colour, with a caramel-like sweetness.
Why is my bellam atukulu sticky?
The poha was soaked or cooked too long. Rinse it for only a few seconds, and take the pan off the heat as soon as every flake is coated.
Why is it made on Krishnashtami?
It recalls the story of Kuchela, who brought a handful of poha to his friend Krishna as his only gift.
